items.title: L&G shareholders approve higher FY26 dividend
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Land & General Bhd's shareholders have approved all nine resolutions at the group's 63rd annual general neeting (AGM) today. Among the resolutions approved was a single-tier final dividend of 0.8 sen per share for the financial year ended March 31, 2026 (FY26). Together with the first interim dividend of 0.2 sen per share paid on May 7, the company's total dividend for FY26 amounts to 1.0 sen per share, 25 per cent higher than the 0.8 sen paid for FY25.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Tuesday, September 22, 2026

items.title: Malaysia reaffirms close partnership with Philippines
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has reaffirmed its close partnership with the Philippines, with cooperation in Asean, trade and investment, and peacebuilding in Mindanao continuing to serve as key pillars of bilateral relations. Malaysian Ambassador to the Philippines Datuk Abdul Malik Melvin Castelino said Malaysia strongly supported the Philippines' 2026 Asean chairmanship under the theme "Navigating Our Future, Together", particularly as the regional grouping begins implementing the Asean 2045: Our Shared Future vision. Speaking at a reception marking Malaysia's 69th National Day in Manila on Monday, he said Malaysia was proud to see its close neighbour carry forward Asean's work at an important time for the region.

items.title: EC awaits official notice on Melaka state assembly dissolution
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Election Commission (EC) has yet to receive official notification regarding the dissolution of the Melaka state legislative assembly. Its chairman, Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun, said a special meeting regarding the state election will be held as soon as the official notification is received. Earlier today, Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh announced that the Melaka state assembly will be dissolved tomorrow.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - September 22, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Negri officials suspended Negri Sembilan has suspended state secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and state legal adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal. Anwar raises plight Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim raised the plight of 55 Malaysians still missing after last month's floods with Nepal's prime minister. Melaka assembly dissolves The Melaka state assembly will be dissolved tomorrow after receiving consent from Yang di-Pertua Negeri Melaka Tun Dr Mohd Ali Mohd Rustam.

items.title: Lawyer: State executive council has no power to suspend Negri top officials
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A lawyer has described the suspension of the Negri Sembilan state secretary and state legal adviser by the state executive council (MMKN) as invalid and without legal effect. Lawyer Muhammad Hariz Md Yusoff said the MMKN had no authority over the services of the state secretary and state Legal Adviser, and that the special meeting at which the decision was made was also invalid. He said the appointments of the state secretary and state legal adviser were made by the Public Service Commission rather than the menteri besar or MMKN.

items.title: Perodua, Bank Rakyat roll out co-branded credit card
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Perusahaan Otomobil Kedua Sdn Bhd (Perodua) and Bank Rakyat have launched a co-branded credit card that offers special benefits for automotive-related spending. The Perodua-Bank Rakyat Credit Card-i is designed to meet vehicle owners' needs by offering reward points that can be easily transferred and redeemed through the Perodua P-Circle app. Bank Rakyat group CEO Ahmad Shahril Mohd Shariff said the strategic partnership with Perodua reflected Bank Rakyat's approach to building an ecosystem that provides customers with more comprehensive value and rewards.

items.title: Indonesia braces for forest, land fire risk into early October as El Nino keeps rainfall low
items.summary: JAKARTA: The risk of forest and land fires is expected to persist in parts of Indonesia into early October, with a very strong El Nino forecast to prolong dry conditions and keep rainfall generally low across much of the country. The Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) said relatively dry atmospheric conditions remained particularly evident in parts of Sumatra and Kalimantan, where high concentrations of hotspots have been detected over the past 10 days alongside reports of forest and land fires. In its 2026-2027 rainy season outlook, BMKG said more than 60 per cent of Indonesia's land area is expected to see the rainy season begin later than the long-term average for the respective regions, with many areas entering the season in November or December.

items.title: Ansara members get extra RM5,000 discount on selected PR1MA homes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The first 200 members of the Association of Former Students of Mara Junior Science College (Ansara) or their family members who purchase selected Perbadanan PR1MA Malaysia (PR1MA) homes will receive an additional RM5,000 discount. PR1MA said the incentive was part of a cooperation agreement signed with Ansara today to expand access to its homeownership opportunities and initiatives for Ansara members and their families. Brian Iskandar said the collaboration reflected PR1MA's commitment to expanding access to homeownership through a network of organisations and communities.

items.title: Thailand on alert as Chao Phraya river water levels expected to rise
items.summary: BANGKOK: Thailand has stepped up preparedness and round-the-clock monitoring of water levels in the Chao Phraya river as an increased water flow is forecast from Sept 29. According to DDPM, the provinces are Uthai Thani, Chai Nat, Sing Buri, Ang Thong, Suphan Buri, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, Lop Buri, Pathum Thani, Nonthaburi and Samut Prakan. However, Theeraphat said the forecast water levels were not expected to affect communities located within designated flood embankment lines.

items.title: Sarawak state assembly's final sitting likely in October — Speaker
items.summary: KUCHING: The Sarawak state assembly's sitting next month is expected to be the final sitting of its current term, said Speaker Tan Sri Mohamad Asfia Awang Nassar. "I will hold a press conference a day before the state assembly sitting and, of course, this will be the final sitting because the current term will end after that. The current term of the Sarawak state assembly will end in February 2027.

items.title: Public urged to stay calm after weak 4.4-magnitude quake off Batu Pahat
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: The public have been advised to remain calm and refrain from spreading unverified information following a weak 4.4-magnitude earthquake detected off Batu Pahat this evening. Batu Pahat district officer Mohd Farid Kassim said the public should refer to the latest updates from reliable sources, including the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) website. Farid, who is also the district Disaster Management Committee chairman, said MetMalaysia reported that the weak earthquake occurred at 4.55pm.

items.title: Thai Customs seize RM870,000 hidden in vehicle at Sadao border
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Thai Customs have seized RM870,000 in Malaysian currency concealed inside a vehicle entering Thailand through the Sadao border checkpoint on Sunday. "Customs officers from the Customs Control Division, Regional Customs Office 4 and Sadao Customs inspected the Thai-registered vehicle and found the cash concealed inside. "The cash, estimated to be worth about 7.1 million baht, was seized under Section 166 of the Thai Customs Act 2017.

items.title: SCIB proposes ESOS of up to 15pct of issued shares to key personnel
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sarawak Consolidated Industries Bhd (SCIB) has announced a proposed employees' share option scheme (ESOS) involving up to 15 per cent of its total issued share capital. Tan, who was appointed as CEO on May 29, and Huang, (appointed COO on May 22), currently hold zero shares in SCIB. The move follows the completion of SCIB's RM113 million cash disposal of its wholly-owned unit, SCIB Concrete Manufacturing Sdn Bhd (SCM), to YTL Cement (Sarawak) Sdn Bhd on May 22.

items.title: UPNM, Ketech Asia to commercialise palm oil-based explosives technology
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is moving to commercialise locally developed palm oil-based technology for the production of explosives and ammunition in a bid to strengthen the country's defence supply chain and reduce reliance on imports. Universiti Pertahanan Nasional Malaysia (UPNM) has signed a memorandum of agreement (MoA) with Ketech Asia Sdn Bhd to bring the university's locally developed technology from the laboratory stage towards large-scale production for use by the defence and security industries. UPNM vice-chancellor Lt Gen Datuk Arman Rumaizi Ahmad said taking the technology from the laboratory to a market-ready stage would require investment, access to specialised testing facilities and industry expertise recognised locally and internationally.

items.title: Haze-related illnesses decline, asthma cases down 35.36pct
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The number of haze-related illness cases declined in Epidemiological Week (EW) 37/2026, with asthma cases registering the largest drop of 35.36 per cent from the previous week, according to the Health Ministry (MOH). In a statement today, the MOH said daily monitoring at 78 haze-specific sentinel health facilities nationwide recorded 722 asthma cases in EW 37/2026, down by 395 cases from 1,117 in EW 36/2026. The ministry said measures included daily monitoring of URTI, asthma and conjunctivitis cases at 78 haze-specific sentinel health facilities, as well as assessing API readings alongside health surveillance data to determine appropriate public health measures.

items.title: Karnival Jom Heboh returns to Miri after 19 years
items.summary: KUCHING: Karnival Jom Heboh (KJH) Sarawak Segulai Sejalai 2026 returns to Miri after 19 years, bringing three days of family entertainment and community activities to Miri Boulevard from Sept 25 to 27. Sports enthusiasts can take part in the EPF Jom Heboh Fun Run Lari Baik-Baik, which returns to Sarawak for the second time, featuring 5km and 8km categories. The carnival will culminate in the U Mobile-sponsored Konsert Jom Heboh Cara U Sarawak Segulai Sejalai 2026 Miri.

items.title: Charges against five Stanford pro-Palestinian protesters to be dismissed
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Charges against five former and current Stanford University students will be dismissed in relation to a 2024 pro-Palestinian demonstration in which protesters barricaded themselves inside the school president's office. California Attorney General Rob Bonta's office said on Monday it would dismiss the charges if the five defendants completed 100 hours of community service each and paid about US$52,000 combined in restitution to the university. Santa Clara County Deputy Public Defender Avi Singh, who represented one of the defendants, said all had "made full restitution and agreed to complete substantial community service so they can move forward with their lives," according to the San Francisco Chronicle.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM SEPT 22, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's 30-stock index closed higher as buying interest returned to banking and healthcare sectors. The key index rose nearly 17 points to close at about 1,683. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Selangor Malay Reserve Land up 1,084.55 hectares since 2018, says Amirudin
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 22 — The total area of Malay Reserve Land in Selangor has increased by 1,084.55 hectares (2,680 acres) since 2018, said Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. In a statement today, Amirudin said the overall area under the state government’s administration had increased from 162,161.98 hectares (400,711 acres) to 163,246.54 hectares (403,391 acres). “Since 2018, the total area of Malay Reserve Land in Selangor under this administration has increased by 1,084.55 hectares (2,680 acres) compared to the previous government,” he said, in response to questions raised regarding the status of Malay Reserve Land in Sabak Bernam.

items.title: Sarawak hopes MA63 commitments reflected in 2027 Budget – Abang Johari
items.summary: Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg said the state government hoped the federal government would continue implementing matters agreed upon under MA63. Asked whether Sarawak expected an increase in allocations under the 2027 Budget, Abang Johari said the matter would depend on the Prime Minister's announcement on Oct 9. "Wait for the Budget.

items.title: More than 10,000 could flee Yemen fighting to Djibouti: UN
items.summary: GENEVA: Renewed fighting in Yemen could see the number of refugees fleeing across the Red Sea to Djibouti jump to 10,000, while displacement inside Yemen could swell to over 230,000, the UN warned Tuesday. The Iran-backed Houthis earlier this month seized control of Yemen's Red Sea coastline, in a dramatic offensive that has left hundreds of people on both sides dead, threatened global trade and pushed up energy prices. "Intensifying fighting in Yemen could drive more mass displacement," United Nations refugee agency spokesman Babar Baloch told reporters in Geneva.

items.title: Sum Technology buys 51pct of security solutions firm INI Technologies for RM2mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sum Technology Bhd is acquiring a 51 per cent stake in security and automation specialist INI Technologies Sdn Bhd for RM2 million cash, expanding beyond its core engineering business. The deal will give Sum Technology access to INI Technologies' electronic security, video surveillance and analytics, access control and automation capabilities. Lee said INI Technologies' technical expertise and relationships with technology partners complemented Sum Technology's mechanical, electrical, process utilities and fire fighting (MEPF) engineering capabilities.

items.title: Just 40m long, new Mont Kiara road opens shortcut to Solaris and Segambut
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — A new road measuring just 40 metres has opened in Mont Kiara, creating a direct connection between Jalan Duta Kiara and Jalan Kiara 3 and giving motorists an alternative route towards Solaris Dutamas, Segambut and surrounding areas. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said Jalan Duta Kiara had previously ended in a dead end, forcing motorists travelling between Bukit Pelangi and Solaris to take a longer route despite the two areas being close to one another. Yeoh said the project followed discussions involving the developer, the Mont Kiara Residents’ Association and other local stakeholders over traffic and connectivity concerns in the area.

items.title: Malay reserve land gazetted out for SABDA development to be replaced – Selangor MB
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The 55.401-acre (about 22.4ha) Malay reserve land in Tanjong Karang, Sabak Bernam, gazetted out for the development of the Sabak Bernam Development Area (SABDA), will be replaced with a tract of the same size in Hulu Selangor. Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the move was aimed at striking a balance between development needs and the preservation of Malay reserve land. He said the 55.401-acre plot in Tanjong Karang, Sabak Bernam, was gazetted out on Sept 3 specifically for the development of SABDA.

items.title: 2027 Budget: Higher allowances proposed for PDK trainers, disabled workers
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry (KPWKM) has proposed higher allowances for disabled workers and staff at Community Rehabilitation Centres (PDK) under the 2027 Budget. Its minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the ministry was committed to ensuring that persons with disabilities (PwD) and those involved in caregiving received appropriate support, particularly to improve their quality of life. Nancy said ahead of the tabling of the 2027 Budget, her ministry also hoped its proposal to strengthen the care economy would be approved.

items.title: MMAG proposes RM130mil capital reduction to erase accumulated losses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MMAG Holdings Bhd has announced a proposed share capital reduction of up to RM130 million to eliminate its accumulated losses and rationalise its financial position, M&A Securities Sdn Bhd, acting as the principal adviser to the group, announced on Sept 22. As of March 31, 2026, MMAG's accumulated losses stood at RM106.77 million. Assuming the maximum credit arising from the capital reduction were set off against the group's accumulated losses, MMAG will record retained earnings of RM23.06 million.

items.title: Pos Malaysia powers up EV deliveries with 1,585 'green' vehicles
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pos Malaysia Bhd says it now delivers one in three parcels using electric vehicles (EVs), as it accelerates the shift towards lower-carbon last-mile delivery The national postal and parcel operator boasts the country's largest electric logistics fleet, comprising 1,253 electric motorcycles and 332 electric vans across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak. Pos Malaysia said the scale of its electrification programme demonstrates how sustainable logistics can be integrated into everyday parcel delivery without changing the way customers send or receive parcels. "Today, we operate Malaysia's largest electric fleet, delivering mail and parcels across the country," he said.

items.title: Sultan Ibrahim consents to new Pulau Aur mosque being used for Friday prayers
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has consented to the newly completed mosque on Pulau Aur being used for Friday prayers for the first time. According to a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar's official Facebook page today, His Majesty also consented to the mosque being named Masjid Zuhri. Also present were Johor Islamic Religious Council chief executive officer Datuk Mohd Radzi Mohd Amin and Teto Engineering Sdn Bhd chairman Datuk Mohd Zuhri Abdullah.

items.title: Mihas 2026 targets RM5bil sales
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The 22nd Malaysia International Halal Showcase (Mihas 2026) is targeting RM5 billion in total sales value, with 50,000 visitors expected to attend the four-day event. Opening tomorrow at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre, Mihas 2026 will bring together 1,700 companies across 2,000 exhibition booths. Mihas' flagship business matching programme, the international sourcing programme, is expected to facilitate 4,000 meetings between 450 international buyers, including 50 premium buyers, with around 600 Malaysian exporters.

items.title: Anwar arrives in Shanghai for 3-day China working visit
items.summary: SHANGHAI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim arrived here today for a three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou aimed at strengthening Malaysia-China ties, boosting trade and expanding cooperation in emerging technologies. The aircraft carrying Anwar and his delegation landed at Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport at 5.10pm local time (5.10pm Malaysian time). Anwar, who is also finance minister, is accompanied by Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.

items.title: Israel minister vows to force out all of Gaza City if any Israeli abducted
items.summary: TEL AVIV: Israel's defence minister vowed Tuesday to force out all of Gaza City's residents and displace a million people in the war-ravaged territory if any Israeli is abducted in the future. Speaking at a memorial for the 1973 Yom Kippur War, Defence Minister Israel Katz also threatened the destruction of infrastructure, which, like the forced displacement of civilians, constitutes a war crime under the Geneva Conventions. Gaza City is home to around 1.1 million people, according to the municipality.

items.title: KPWKM seeks higher Budget 2027 allowances for disabled workers and PDK staff, says Nancy
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 22 — The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry (KPWKM) has proposed higher allowances for disabled workers and staff at Community Rehabilitation Centres (PDK) under Budget 2027, the minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said. She said the ministry was committed to ensuring that persons with disabilities (PwD) and those involved in caregiving received appropriate support, particularly to improve their quality of life. Nancy said ahead of the tabling of Budget 2027, her ministry also hoped its proposal to strengthen the care economy would be approved.

items.title: MCMC ready to license e-commerce platforms once ministries set conditions, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — The Communications Ministry is waiting for the terms and conditions from the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) and the Finance Ministry (MoF) before licensing e-commerce platforms. Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has the power under the existing legal framework to license the platforms, but the specific conditions must be decided by the relevant ministries. MCMC, or the Ministry of Communications, is involved because under the Malaysian legal framework, we have the power to actually license e-commerce platforms.

items.title: Magnitude 4.4 earthquake detected off Batu Pahat, tremors felt onshore
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Sept 22 — A magnitude 4.4 earthquake was detected off the coast of Batu Pahat at 4.55pm today. The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said the earthquake struck at a depth of 10 kilometres, with its epicentre at 1.7 degrees north and 102.7 degrees east, about 27 kilometres southwest of Batu Pahat. Tremors were felt in Batu Pahat and surrounding areas, MetMalaysia said, adding that it would continue to monitor the situation.

items.title: Sarawak’s next legislative assembly sitting will be the last of current term, says state Speaker
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 22 — The coming Sarawak Legislative Assembly (DUN) will be the last one for this term, said Speaker Tan Sri Datuk Amar Mohamad Asfia Awang Nassar. However, he said the dates of the coming DUN sitting have not been announced yet. So, I will call a press conference before the DUN,” said Asfia.

items.title: Anwar arrives in Shanghai for three-day working visit
items.summary: SHANGHAI, Sept 22 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim arrived here on Tuesday for a three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou, China, aimed at strengthening Malaysia-China ties, boosting trade and expanding cooperation in emerging technologies. Also present were Shanghai Vice-Mayor of Shanghai Wang Huajie, China’s Ambassador to Malaysia Ouyang Yujing, and Su Lin, a member of the Party Leadership Group of the Shanghai Municipal Foreign Affairs Office. Anwar, who is also finance minister, is accompanied by Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry, Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, and Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.

items.title: Melaka to keep running as usual as state assembly heads for dissolution
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 22 — Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has given assurance that the Melaka state government’s affairs will continue to run as usual even though the Melaka State Legislative Assembly (DUN) is dissolved effective tomorrow. He said the state administration, public service delivery, public welfare affairs, security and the government’s daily services will continue to operate as usual. “Following this dissolution, the state government will carry out its responsibilities in the capacity of a caretaker government until a new state government is formed after the election process.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan govt suspends state secretary, legal adviser amid royal row
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — The Negeri Sembilan government today suspended the state secretary and state legal adviser with immediate effect amid the ongoing dispute involving the state’s royal institution. The two officials are State Secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and State Legal Adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal. In a statement, Ismail said State Financial Officer Datuk Masri Razali would assume the duties of the state secretary until a new state secretary is appointed by the Chief Secretary to the Government.

items.title: Tasik Bera enforcement: Five arrested, investigation papers to be referred to DPP
items.summary: Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the reports were lodged by members of the Orang Asli community and enforcement personnel. Azry Akmar said the investigation papers on five individuals arrested on Sept 15 for allegedly obstructing enforcement officers during the operation would be referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor soon. In an unrelated development, Azry Akmar said police had opened two investigation papers following a recent altercation at a religious school in Bukit Ibam, Rompin.

items.title: PKR’s Hassan Karim urges Anwar to retain Anthony Loke ahead of major transport projects
items.summary: PASIR GUDANG, Sept 22 — Pasir Gudang MP Hassan Abdul Karim has called on Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to persuade Anthony Loke to remain as transport minister to ensure the completion of several key infrastructure projects, including those in Johor. The PKR lawmaker expressed concern that Loke’s resignation could jeopardise ongoing projects, including those in Johor. “I hope the prime minister takes my view into consideration and persuades Loke to stay.

items.title: As parents age, Malaysia must plan for neurodivergent adults too, says Nancy Shukri
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Planning for neurodivergent individuals must extend beyond childhood intervention to cover their needs throughout their lifespan, particularly as their parents and caregivers grow older. Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said this was increasingly important as neurodivergent individuals were living longer and Malaysia was rapidly transitioning towards an ageing society, with those aged 60 and above expected to make up 15 per cent of the population by 2036. She said disability planning had traditionally focused on early intervention and childhood development, but this needed to be expanded to address the long-term needs of neurodivergent individuals and ageing caregivers.

items.title: Malaysia’s research has potential, now it needs to leave the lab, says higher education minister
items.summary: Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the milestone demonstrated Malaysia’s immense capacity for innovation, provided the gap between academic research and commercial market demands could be bridged effectively. “Malaysia had many good researchers, ideas and promising innovations, but too many of them remained at the university level. “For the first time, we are creating a dedicated platform for university researchers to bring their ideas directly to industry, investors and potential partners,” he said during the opening ceremony of the University Research and Innovation Investment Summit 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre here today.

items.title: No drug arrests for a week? Kelantan police chief says two station heads get reprimand letters
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 22 — Two police station chiefs (OCSs) in Kelantan have received reprimand letters after they failed to record any drug-related arrests for a week, said state police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat. He said the state police headquarters is monitoring seven police stations with regard to enforcement against drug abuse and trafficking. Mohd Yusoff said the performance of each police station is monitored weekly and presented at meetings with the head of the Narcotics Department.

items.title: Finance pros cannot escape geopolitics in a changing world, says deputy finance minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Finance professionals must adapt to a rapidly changing global landscape shaped by geopolitical shifts, climate and sustainability challenges, artificial intelligence (AI) and growing concerns over trust. Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said the transformation of the global environment in recent years had created new challenges for businesses and finance professionals, requiring them to rethink how financial systems and structures are designed. As such, he emphasised the need for financial professionals to understand geopolitical developments worldwide, particularly as businesses face growing risks to investment, technology and supply chains.

items.title: Melaka heads for polls as CM Rauf Yusoh confirms assembly set for dissolution tomorrow
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 22 — The Melaka State Legislative Assembly will be dissolved tomorrow to pave the way for the 16th state election. Ab Rauf said State Assembly Speaker Datuk Ibrahim Durum had also submitted the notice of dissolution to the Election Commission (EC). They were former Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Idris Haron (BN-Sungai Udang), Datuk Nor Azman Hassan (BN-Pantai Kundor), Datuk Noor Effandi Ahmad (Bersatu-Telok Mas) and independent Datuk Norhizam Hassan Baktee (Pengkalan Batu).

items.title: Three actors out on bail as police hunt uploader of viral Rukun Negara clip from 2018
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Bukit Aman have released three local actors on police bail after questioning them over a viral video of a 2018 theatre performance allegedly mocking the Rukun Negara, while investigators hunt for the person who re-uploaded the footage. “The three have since been released on police bail after their statements were recorded, and checks found no content from the performance on their mobile phones or other devices. The performing arts centre has since closed, Kumar said.

items.title: From ‘Made in Malaysia’ to ‘Made by Malaysia’: Govt wants R&D to turn more research into commercial gains
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — The government is looking to strengthen Malaysia’s research and development (R&D) ecosystem through more market-driven funding mechanisms and closer industry collaboration, said Minister of Finance II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. He said Malaysia is shifting from a “Made in Malaysia” to a “Made by Malaysia” approach as it seeks to strengthen value creation and drive economic upgrading, with R&D playing a central role. While Malaysia’s R&D spending has reached about one per cent of gross domestic product, or nearly RM20 billion, he said the main challenge is turning research into commercial results.

items.title: After retiring as police No 2, Ayob Khan takes on new role as UTeM board chairman
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 22 — Former Deputy Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay has been appointed chairman of the Universiti Teknikal Malaysia Melaka (UTeM) Board of Directors for a three-year term effective Sept 16. The university said Ayob Khan’s extensive experience in leadership and senior management in one of the country’s key departments was expected to strengthen the UTeM Board’s role in steering the university’s strategic direction sustainably. “UTeM believes his extensive experience and strong strategic management credentials will enable him to lead the UTeM Board in addressing the challenges ahead,” it said.

items.title: Piranha in Pahang? Fisheries Department calls in Aquaria KLCC for DNA backup
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 22 — The Department of Fisheries Malaysia (DOF) will collaborate with Aquaria KLCC to identify fish suspected to be piranhas at Klau Dam, Raub, Pahang, using DNA or environmental DNA (eDNA) analysis. Director-General of Fisheries Datuk Adnan Hussain said the collaboration would leverage live piranha specimens and existing DNA data held by Aquaria KLCC to determine the fish’s identity. Adnan said the Pahang Fisheries Department had instructed inland fishermen at Klau Dam to retain and surrender any fish resembling piranhas for examination of their morphology, scales and teeth.

items.title: Zahid: Neither MB Ismail Lasim nor I was summoned by Negeri Sembilan Ruler for an audience
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said neither he nor Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim was summoned for an audience with Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir at Istana Negeri Sembilan here yesterday. Neither the Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar nor I was ever summoned for an audience. The institutions and establishment in Negeri Sembilan must also be respected,” he said.

items.title: Melaka heads for polls? CM Ab Rauf set to make big announcement today
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 22 — Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh is expected to announce the dissolution of the Melaka State Legislative Assembly at 2pm today, paving the way for the 16th state election. Speculation over an imminent dissolution intensified after the state executive council meeting, usually held on Wednesdays, was brought forward by a day. In the 2021 Melaka state election, Barisan Nasional (BN) won 21 of the 28 seats contested, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) secured five and Perikatan Nasional (PN) two.

items.title: Passenger falls onto tracks at Wangsa Maju LRT station after reportedly fainting
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — A passenger reportedly fainted before falling onto the tracks at the Wangsa Maju LRT station this morning, causing a brief disruption to services on the Kelana Jaya line. Rapid KL said the incident occurred at 6.52am. The passenger was rescued from the track area by station personnel and taken to the emergency department for immediate treatment, Rapid KL said.

items.title: Bukit Aman: Eight minors, two civil servants among 53 arrested over child sexual abuse materials
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Eight minors aged between 13 and 18 were among dozens arrested for possessing child child sexual abuse materials (CSAM) in a joint operation by Bukit Aman’s Criminal Investigation Department and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar told a press conference here that the minors were being investigated for possessing and selling animated CSAM made using artificial intelligence (AI), describing it as a “worrying trend”. “What is most worrying about this is that among those arrested were minors and civil servants,” he said today.

items.title: Miti says Bumiputera equity policy is not under its purview but Economy Ministry’s
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — The Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (Miti) today clarified that it has no information regarding matters related to the Bumiputera equity ownership policy. Miti said the matter falls under the purview of the Ministry of Economy. The statement was issued following a media statement by the Ministry of Education on Sept 21 regarding the standardisation of ownership requirements for private educational institutions under the ministry.

items.title: Leatherback makes third Terengganu landing this month, lays 70 eggs
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Sept 22 — The Department of Fisheries Malaysia (DOF), through the Rantau Abang Turtle and Marine Ecosystem Centre (TCIC), recorded three leatherback turtle (Dermochelys coriacea) landings along the Terengganu coast this month, involving 195 eggs that were transferred to a controlled incubation site for protection. Director-General of Fisheries Datuk Adnan Hussain said the records provide important data to monitor leatherback turtle landings, protect the eggs and improve their survival chances. The first nesting was recorded at Pasir Putih Beach, Marang, on Sept 1, involving 44 eggs, followed by 81 eggs at Rantau Abang Beach on Sept 13 and 70 eggs at Kuala Abang Beach today.

items.title: Kelantan investment manager loses RM1.2m in savings and jewellery after scammers spoof police phone number
items.summary: Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the woman, a single mother in her 50s, received a call from an individual posing as an authority and claiming that she was involved in a money laundering case. Mohd Yusoff said the syndicate also used application spoofing technology to make the phone number appear as though the call was from the police, including using the Kelantan IPK’s telephone number. He said police detected about 68 calls a day using the Kelantan IPK’s number, and the matter was now under investigation.

items.title: Penang wants more than tourist numbers as it shifts to high-value tourism
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 22 — Penang is seeking the federal government’s support through Budget 2027 to strengthen its tourism agenda, including improving air connectivity, attracting more international events and preserving George Town’s heritage. State Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said the priorities were aimed at increasing the value of the tourism sector while ensuring its growth continued to benefit the local economy and community. Wong said Penang was also seeking a larger federal matching fund to bid for and attract international conferences, exhibitions, sporting events, festivals, concerts, as well as large-scale arts and cultural events.

items.title: Uncle remanded seven days over death of five-year-old girl allegedly thrown into Johor river
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 22 — A 37-year-old man who allegedly threw his five-year-old niece into a river in Kampung Padang, Tanjung Sedili here, causing her death yesterday, has been remanded for seven days to assist in the investigation. It was reported yesterday that police arrested a local man for allegedly throwing his niece into a river, resulting in her death. Kota Tinggi police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said police received a report at about 9.30am before arresting the suspect.

items.title: Beyond minimum wage, Malaysia needs clearer wage ladders tied to productivity, says Akmal Nasrullah
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 22 — Wage compression is hindering working Malaysians from receiving proper compensation despite the narrowing wage gap between low- and semi-skilled workers in Malaysia, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said today. Citing a recent Bank Negara report, Akmal Nasrullah said the wage difference between low- and semi-skilled workers had narrowed from RM550 in 2016 to RM396 in 2024. As such, he said raising the floor wage was only a starting point and the ministry must develop clearer wage ladders that keep pace with productivity.
